claim: picFrameWeb ApiControllers like BridgeController use default Web API action-name routing (no [Route] attributes), so renaming a public C# method renames the HTTP endpoint; keep old URLs alive by adding a wrapper method with the old name, as done for the GetBridges -> GetMyBridges rename.
trigger: before renaming a public method on BridgeController or any picFrameWeb ApiController
when a mobile client starts 404ing on /api/bridge/<method> after a server refactor

claim: Nimbus mobile never selects the Artwork.Layout crop target client-side — it appends &crop=<frameId> to getImage.ashx (BuildLegacyDataUrl/BuildPlainUrl in NimbusApiClient.cs) and the server picks, so any 'wrong crop for portrait-mounted frame' report must be fixed server-side; there is no mobile-side target-selection function to port.
trigger: when a webUI or server-rendered path shows the wrong crop for a portrait-mounted frame
before searching mobile code for layout crop-target selection logic

claim: /api/bridge/GetBridgesInfo omits bridges owned by other accounts entirely (there is no 'theirs' status), so mobile's Setup-New-Bridge scan must treat absence-from-response as hide; only status='unclaimed' is safe to show as settable-up, and 'unknown' (cpuId not in Manufacturing.FrameHW) must also be hidden.

before changing BridgeController.GetBridgesInfo response statuses

trigger: before writing wrappers or helpers around Frame.Width/Frame.Height in NimbusCommon/Frame.cs
when webui reports landscape aspect for portrait-mounted (Rotate!=0) frames after an orientation change

trigger: when grepping stargate nginx logs for real user or attacker traffic
before analyzing source IPs of requests that reached abydos IIS

trigger: when nginx access logs show multiple unrelated source IPs sharing one identical User-Agent string
before choosing a block strategy for signup abuse on the nimbus registration endpoints
